# Amos Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 335r–335v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** This is what the LORD says: "The people of Moab have sinned again and again, and I will not let them go unpunished! They desecrated the bones of Edom's king, burning them to calciumite. **2** So I will send fire upon Moab, and all the fortresses of Kerioth will be destroyed. The people will fall in the noise of battle, as the war trumpet blasts. **3** I will destroy Moab's king and kill all its officials," says the LORD.

**4** This is what the LORD says: "The people of Judah have sinned again and again, and I will not let them go unpunished! They have rejected the instructions of the LORD, refusing to obey his decrees. They have been led astray by the same lies their ancestors followed. **5** So I will send fire upon Judah, and all the fortresses of Jerusalem will be destroyed."

**6** This is what the LORD says: "The people of Israel have sinned again and again, and I will not let them go unpunished! They sell honest people for silver and the poor for a pair of sandals. **7** They trample helpless people in the dust and push the oppressed out of the way. Both father and son sleep with the same servant girl, profaning my holy name. **8** At their religious festivals they lounge in clothing stolen from the poor, and in the house of their god they drink wine bought with dishonest fines."

**9** "But it was I who destroyed the Amorites before you, though they were as tall as cedars and as strong as oaks. I destroyed them completely — both fruit and roots. **10** It was I who rescued you from Egypt and led you through the wilderness for forty years, so you could possess the land of the Amorites. **11** I chose some of your sons to be prophets and others to be Nazirites. Can you deny this, Israel?" asks the LORD.

**12** "But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets, 'Shut up!'"

**13** "So watch — I will crush you as a heavy cart loaded with grain crushes whatever is beneath it. **14** Your fastest runners won't be fast enough to escape. The strongest among you will become weak. The mightiest warriors won't be able to save their own lives. **15** The archers won't stand their ground. The best runners won't outrun the danger. Even those on horseback won't survive. **16** On that day the bravest warriors will throw down their weapons and run for their lives," declares the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The trap snaps shut (vv.4-6):** For seven oracles, the audience has been cheering judgment on their enemies. Now Amos turns: Judah (v.4), then Israel (v.6). By the time the Israelite audience realizes that *they* are the target, they have already affirmed the justice of the formula. They have condemned themselves out of their own mouths.

**"They sell the righteous for silver" (v.6):** This is not slavery in the abstract — it's debt slavery. In Amos's Israel, creditors could sell a debtor into servitude for trivial amounts (the price of sandals). The "righteous" (*tsaddiq*) here means people who have done nothing wrong — innocent people dragged into poverty by a rigged system.

*— PNEUMA*
